objectives.label: Noticed the silence follows the stones
Sang a route-song verse at the relay

facet_depot.name: The Depot Stone
facet_depot.text: Its depot tag still says 'Strongbox 9. SOLD.' It rings like a dinner bell.

verses_relay_spiral.name: The Spiral Verses
verses_relay_spiral.text: New route-song verses on bark. Sung in order, the roads curl around the gemfalls.

scene_north_roads.narration: North of the west branch, the road splits into two lanes. The upbound lane is the rush going up: wagons, picks, and people singing. The downbound lane is the rush coming back: slower, quieter, carrying a lot less than it set out with. Everybody is talking at once.

choices.label: Fall in with the northbound traffic
Ride north with the drovers from the ford
Climb up out of the marsh, muddy and wagonless

scene_north_roads_fall_in.narration: You fall in between a wagon full of picks and a wagon full of pickles. Nobody knows you, nobody minds you, and everybody is singing a different song. A man with a parrot tells you the Gemfall is two days north. The parrot says three. They argue about it for a mile.

choices.label: Roll on north

scene_drovers_wagon.narration: The lead drover from the ford spots you and booms, "Mudlarks! Up you get!" It is what he calls everybody he likes. You ride the tailboard of a gem wagon with your legs dangling, eating dried apples, while the whole queue rolls north like one long creaking animal.

choices.label: Roll on north

scene_out_of_marsh.narration: You come up out of the marsh reeds onto the road with mud to your knees and the boggarts' hum still in your ears. Nobody on the road has a seat for you, so you work your passage: carrying water buckets for a wagon that smells strongly of turnips. The boggarts, somewhere behind you, are laughing.

choices.label: Carry your buckets north

scene_jackalope_race.narration: Out on the open road, jackalopes are everywhere: little antlered hares racing the wagons for fun, and winning. One of them lopes alongside you, looks you up and down, and thumps the road twice with a back foot. On the Plains, everybody knows what that means. It is a challenge.

choices.label: Race it to the next mile marker
Cheer for the wagon horses instead
Race it from the air

check_jackalope_race.prompt: Race a jackalope to the mile marker

onSuccess.narration: You run like the wind and lose by one ear, which is the best anybody has done all season. The jackalope looks you over with new respect and thumps once. That means friends. It lopes along beside you for the next mile, showing off.

onFailure.narration: You run like the wind. The jackalope runs like a much faster wind, then sits at the mile marker cleaning its antlers until you catch up. It thumps once anyway, as if to say: nice try. Then it is off to race a cart.

scene_jackalope_race_cheer.narration: You cheer the wagon horses on, and the horses try their very best. The jackalope wins by a mile, turns round, and runs the whole race again backwards, just to make a point. The drivers laugh. "That's the Plains," one says. "The jackalopes always win. Always. Everywhere."

choices.label: Walk on up the road

scene_jackalope_race_fly.narration: Your griffin takes off and races it from above. The jackalope zigzags, doubles back, and dives under a wagon. Nobody wins, which by jackalope rules means you are now best friends. It lopes along under your shadow for the next mile, thumping happily.

choices.label: Walk on up the road

scene_empty_stretch.narration: Plains folk say an empty stretch of good road is a message, and jackalopes are the punctuation. Normally they are everywhere, racing wagons and winning. But for a whole mile around the big gem depot up ahead, the warrens have gone completely silent, and the road feels like a sentence with the end missing.

choices.label: Count the jackalopes, and where they stop
Notice the silence moving with your own pack
Watch the jackalope you raced
Keep walking toward the depot

scene_empty_stretch_racer.narration: Your jackalope friend is still loping beside you. Then, at one particular stone, it stops dead. It thumps the road three times, hard, and will not take one more step, not toward the depot and not toward your packs. It is not the road it is worried about. It is what you are carrying.

choices.label: Look at your packs

scene_empty_stretch_keep_walking.narration: You keep walking. The mile is very quiet: no thumps, no rustles, not one antler in the grass. Even the wagon drivers stop singing. Somebody's horse keeps looking back over its shoulder, as if it has heard something you cannot.

choices.label: Walk on to the downbound lane

check_jackalopes.prompt: Count the jackalopes and find where they stop

onSuccess.narration: You count forty-one, forty-two, forty-three, and then none. Not one. The last jackalope sits exactly at the edge of the silence like a full stop, and you can draw the line from where you stand.

onFailure.narration: You get to forty-one jackalopes, and then one of them sits up and stares at you until you lose count. It has won. You do not know what, but it has definitely won.

scene_silence_follows.narration: You notice it all at once: the warrens go quiet around the depot, and around the gem wagons, and around YOU. Every jackalope within shouting distance of a stone has gone underground. It is not the eruption the land is flinching from. It is the stones.

choices.label: Walk on, a little quieter

scene_downbound.narration: On the downbound lane, a sold-out prospector called Ma Ruddle is watching her own wagon being auctioned. "I don't care about the wagon," she says. "I've lost my nephew Tib in this crowd. Small. Orange hat. Talks to horses."

choices.label: Work the crowd like a stage
Fly up and look for an orange hat
Ask the centaur relay to pass the word
Search the crowd yourselves

scene_downbound_fly_look.narration: You go up. From above, the crowd is a river of hats, all of them brown or gray or straw, except one. One orange dot, standing perfectly still beside a pony, talking.

choices.label: Land next to the orange dot

scene_downbound_work_crowd.narration: Your kitsune climbs onto an upturned crate and announces, in a voice like a town crier, "LOST! ONE SMALL BOY! ORANGE HAT! TALKS TO HORSES!" The whole downbound lane stops to listen. Then forty people point in the same direction at once.

choices.label: Follow the pointing

check_relay.prompt: Explain Tib to a centaur at a full gallop

onSuccess.narration: The runner nods, sings "small, orange hat, talks to horses" to the next runner, and in less time than it takes to eat a honeycake the word comes back down the line: found.

onFailure.narration: The runner hears "small orange horse" and gallops off. Much later, word comes back that Tib turned up by himself, talking to a centaur. Ma Ruddle's thanks are tired, and her papers went in the auction pile.

check_search.prompt: Dodge through a very busy crowd after a small orange hat

onSuccess.narration: You spot the hat, lose it behind a wagon, spot it again, and finally find Tib explaining something very seriously to a pony.

onFailure.narration: Every time you get close, the orange hat turns out to be a pumpkin. Much later the relay finds Tib on its own, and Ma Ruddle's papers have gone in the auction pile.

scene_tib_found.narration: Tib is found, still holding a long conversation with a pony. Ma Ruddle hugs him so hard his hat falls off. Then she pulls a folded paper from her boot. "Bill of sale for the stone I left at the depot. I'm going home. You have it."

choices.label: Thank her and walk on down the lane

scene_stubborn_mule.narration: Farther down the downbound lane, nobody is moving at all. A mule has sat down in the middle of the road with a gem sack on its back, and it will not get up. Its owner is pleading, the wagons behind are shouting, and the mule is calmly chewing a daisy, as if none of this is its problem.

choices.label: Push the mule up onto its feet
Take the sack off and carry it yourselves
Kneel down and feel what the mule feels

check_push_mule.prompt: Shift a mule that has decided not to move

onSuccess.narration: You heave together, and the gem sack slips off the mule's back in the struggle. The moment it hits the ground, the mule leaps up, fresh as morning, and trots three steps away from it. "She'll carry anything," says the owner, amazed. "Anything but that, it seems."

onFailure.narration: You push. The mule leans. The mule wins, and you all sit down in the road in a heap. From down there you notice the mule is not glaring at you at all. It is glaring at the gem sack on its own back. Its owner sees it too, and slowly takes the sack off.

scene_stubborn_mule_unload.narration: You lift the gem sack off. The mule springs up at once, brays a thank you, and trots off with its ears high. The sack hums in your arms all the way to some big tents by the roadside, where you hand it back to its very puzzled owner. Your arms ache. The mule waves its ears at you from the roadside.

choices.label: Head for the tents by the road

scene_stubborn_mule_ask_mule.narration: Your unicorn kneels by the mule and goes quiet. The mule is not stubborn. It is uneasy, the way you feel before a thunderstorm, when the sky has not done anything yet. And the feeling is coming from the sack. Your unicorn says so, gently, and the owner takes the sack off without another word.

choices.label: Head for the tents by the road

rest_soup_tents.narration: Beside the downbound lane, people in dark robes with little humming crystals on strings have put up rest tents, with DEEP HOLLOW stitched small on the flaps: three of them, with cots and blankets and hot bowls for anyone the rush has dropped. The ladler is called Wend, and Wend has all your names by the second bowl, and says them as if they had always been known.

choices.label: Listen to what Wend wants to say
Thank everyone and get back on the road

rest_soup_tents_rest_go.narration: You thank everybody, fold your blankets, and get back on the road. Wend waves you off with the ladle. "Come back any time," Wend calls. "We'll still be here. We're always here now." Behind you, the robed folk are putting up a fourth tent.

choices.label: Back on the road

scene_wend_pitch.narration: "The world's a little bit broken, isn't it?" Wend says gently. "Wrong-colored sky, humming stones. We think it could be fixed, right at the root." Wend's crystal hums the same note as the stones. "Would you carry a letter north for us? Just a letter." By the soup pot sits a little wooden box with a slot in the lid.

choices.label: Say no thank you, kindly but clearly
Say maybe, and leave it there
Drop a coin in the box, for the soup

scene_wend_pitch_say_later.narration: "Maybe," you say. Wend nods as if maybe is a kind of yes, and slides a folded letter into the top of your pack "in case you change your minds." It is sealed with a drop of something that glitters. You can feel it in there for the rest of the day, like a stone in a boot.

choices.label: Back on the road

scene_wend_pitch_say_no.narration: "No, thank you," you say, kindly and clearly. Wend smiles exactly as warmly as before, which is somehow the strangest part. "Kindness first anyway," says Wend, and tucks a warm bread roll into the nearest pack "for the road." The crystal keeps humming.

choices.label: Back on the road

scene_wend_pitch_coin.narration: You drop a coin in the little wooden box. The lid says FOR THE ROOT OF THINGS. Wend's crystal hums louder for a moment, like a hive woken up. "Kindness first," says Wend softly, and writes your names in a small book with a soft pencil. You are not quite sure what you just paid for.

choices.label: Back on the road

scene_road_crew.narration: Up ahead, a crew of centaurs is moving the road. Not mending it: moving it. They pull up old marker posts and plant new ones in a long curve through the grass, around a scorched hollow where a fallen stone once lay. "Third detour this month," puffs the road boss, a post on each shoulder. "Lend a hand?"

choices.label: Haul marker posts with the crew
Ask why the road keeps moving
Hold Mother Thrum's charm over the hollow
Fly up and look at the shape of the detours

check_haul_posts.prompt: Carry marker posts for a centaur road crew

onSuccess.narration: You carry posts until your arms feel like noodles, and you plant every one straight. The road boss looks down the new curve and nods. "Good work. The relay will sing about this," she says, and she does not sound like she is joking.

onFailure.narration: You carry a post the wrong way round and plant it upside down, so the arrow points at the sky. The crew decides this is very funny and leaves it there, as a joke for the next runner. The road boss thanks you anyway, still chuckling.

scene_road_crew_ask_why.narration: The road boss leans on a post. "A stone fell here, the red night. Since then nothing will walk past this hollow. Not horses, not hares. The grass won't even lean toward it. So the road goes round. A road always goes where the walking goes." She glances at your packs, and then away.

choices.label: Walk the new curve north

scene_road_crew_charm.narration: You hold the tuned charm out over the scorched hollow. It sings, faint and thin, though the stone that fell here was carried off weeks ago. The ground still remembers it. The whole crew stops work to stare. "Well," says the road boss slowly. "That would explain a thing or two."

choices.label: Walk the new curve north

scene_road_crew_fly.narration: From up high you can see it: this is not the only detour. All along the north roads, little curves of new posts bend away from scorched hollows, one after another, like somebody walking carefully round puddles. The road is not wandering. It is stepping around something.

choices.label: Land and walk the new curve

scene_warden_patrol.narration: A Skywarden supply patrol has stopped the road: silver and violet armor, very neat ledgers. Sergeant Holloway is requisitioning food at fixed rates for Redspire, the wardens' citadel up in the foothills. Everybody around you is calling it theft. Sergeant Holloway is calling it arithmetic.

choices.label: Pay the fixed rate and wish them well
Argue that the rate is unfair
Swap sky news, griffin to warden

scene_warden_patrol_griffin_logs.narration: Your griffin and the sergeant swap sky news the way old flyers do: wind at the bridge, ash over the mountain, a storm sitting on the sea that will not come in. Holloway writes all of it down and reads it back twice. "Useful," the sergeant says, and waves the patrol aside to let you through.

choices.label: On toward the depot

scene_warden_patrol_pay.narration: You pay the fixed rate. Sergeant Holloway writes PAID, POLITE in the ledger and hands you a receipt, then a copy of the receipt, then a receipt for the copy. "Arithmetic," the sergeant says, almost kindly. "It's the only thing up here that isn't shouting."

choices.label: On toward the depot

onSuccess.narration: You find a mistake in the sergeant's sums. Sergeant Holloway checks it twice, corrects it, and pays you back two coppers with deep respect.

onFailure.narration: Sergeant Holloway listens to your whole argument, writes it down in the ledger under 'Complaints, Polite', and charges you the fixed rate anyway.

scene_signposts.narration: Where the road forks, somebody has nailed up forty signs that all say GEMS THIS WAY, and they all point different ways. Under them, a man in a velvet coat is selling maps to the Gemfall. "Two coppers each! Guaranteed accurate, or your money back from my cousin," he says, "who has left."

choices.label: Buy one of his maps
Work out which signs are honest
Beat the map seller at his own game

check_read_signs.prompt: Sort the honest signs from the nonsense

onSuccess.narration: Most of the signs are nonsense. But a few old, weathered ones, nailed up by the relay, all agree about one thing: the road north bends away from every place a stone came down. You follow the honest arrows straight to the depot.

onFailure.narration: You follow the most convincing sign for half an hour and arrive at a pig farm. The pigs are friendly. The farmer points you back toward the depot, and politely waits until you are out of sight before he laughs.

scene_signposts_buy_map.narration: You buy a map. It is beautifully drawn. It is also, when you turn it the right way up, a drawing of a duck. By the time you notice, the velvet coat has moved to a different fork. You keep the duck anyway. It is a very good duck.

choices.label: Ask a wagon driver the way to the depot

scene_signposts_outsell.narration: Your kitsune sets up right next to him, selling maps that say, honestly, ASK A CENTAUR. They sell out in ten minutes. The man in the velvet coat is so impressed that he buys one himself. Then he packs up his maps and goes off to ask a centaur.

choices.label: Follow the honest arrows to the depot

scene_depot.narration: The biggest rush depot on the north roads is a barn full of strongboxes, and one of them is ringing like a bell. Behind the counter sits Clerk Pennywhistle, who has a queue, a stamp, and a form for absolutely everything, including a form for asking about forms. The ringing stone is in strongbox number nine.

choices.label: Hand over Ma Ruddle's bill of sale
Queue up and fill in the forms properly
Leave it in the strongbox and head on

check_forms.prompt: Fill in Form 9 with no smudges, in the right order

onSuccess.narration: Clerk Pennywhistle holds your form up to the lamp, finds no smudges, and looks as if he might cry with happiness. He stamps it four times.

onFailure.narration: You fill in Form 9. It needed Form 7B first. Clerk Pennywhistle is very sorry. The queue behind you is not.

scene_strongbox.narration: Clerk Pennywhistle unlocks strongbox number nine, lifts out a gem that rings like a dinner bell, and writes your names in the depot ledger in lovely handwriting. "The Depot Stone," he reads off the tag. "Sold. Please keep it away from my pens."

choices.label: Walk on to the noon stop

scene_depot_leave.narration: You leave the ringing stone in strongbox number nine. Clerk Pennywhistle looks enormously relieved and stamps something to celebrate. As you go out, the strongbox rings after you, one long note, and every pen on his counter rattles in its pot.

choices.label: Walk on to the noon stop

scene_rumor_fire.narration: At the noon stop, a ring of travelers is swapping news, and the news has clearly been swapped a great many times. "On the River Road," says one, "a troll charges you a story instead of a coin." "On the Wild Road," says another, "the marsh steals your boots and gives back different boots." Everybody turns to you. "What's your news?"

choices.label: Tell the tallest tale you can
Tell them the true thing: the gems all hum
Tell them about the two-day queue at the ford
Tell them what the marsh is really like

check_tall_tale.prompt: Tell a tall tale the whole ring believes

onSuccess.narration: You tell them you rode a river drake across the ford, sideways, wearing a hat. By the end the whole ring believes you, and three people are already retelling it with a bigger hat. By nightfall, the hat has feathers.

onFailure.narration: You start well, but you mix up the drake with the river, and the river with your aunt. The ring laughs kindly and decides your aunt must be a river. That rumor will be all over the Plains by Tuesday.

scene_rumor_fire_true_news.narration: You tell them plainly: every gem on the road hums the same note. The ring goes quiet. Then an old woman says, "My nephew on the River Road said a troll told him the very same." A boy says, "My cousin heard it from a boggart." Three roads, one note. Nobody says anything for a while.

choices.label: Walk on into the evening

scene_rumor_fire_ford_news.narration: You tell them about the two-day queue, the numbered pebbles, Burdock's goat with a bucket on her head, and the drovers singing the crossing verse. The ring gasps in all the right places. By sunset the story has gone up and down the road twice and come back with three extra goats.

choices.label: Walk on into the evening

scene_rumor_fire_marsh_news.narration: You tell them the marsh does not steal boots. The boggarts only borrow things, and keep very careful records, and hum. The ring is fascinated. One man takes off his boots and looks at them suspiciously. Somewhere far behind you, you are sure, a boggart is laughing.

choices.label: Walk on into the evening

scene_bell_courier.narration: Toward evening, a small dragonling on a fat pony comes trotting down from the north, ringing a hand bell in a pattern: ding, ding, pause, ding. She stops to let the pony drink, puffing. "News from the boundary stones," she says. "Can't stop long. Got to ring it all the way to the river."

choices.label: Offer to ring the pattern while she rests
Ask what the news is
Ring her an answer, the way they do at home

check_ring_pattern.prompt: Ring a bell pattern exactly right

onSuccess.narration: Ding, ding, pause, ding. You get it exactly right, and far away to the south, very faintly, another bell rings it back. The courier beams. "You'd make a grandmother one day," she says, which is the biggest compliment she knows.

onFailure.narration: Ding, pause, ding, ding, ding. The courier goes pink. "That one means the cake is ready," she whispers. Far to the south, a whole camp sits down hopefully to wait for cake. She takes the bell back, giggling, and rings it properly.

scene_bell_courier_ask_news.narration: "The grandmothers are turning pry bars back at the boundary stones," she says. "Whole wagonloads. And they say anybody carrying a stone that hums should come and see them first." She looks hard at your packs. "Like yours." Then she is back on the pony, bell going, before you can ask her how she knew.

choices.label: Head for the relay campfire

scene_bell_courier_ring_back.narration: You take the bell and ring the answer every dragonling child knows: heard you, coming home. The courier's mouth falls open. "You're from the hills!" she squeaks. "Oh, the grandmothers will want YOU." She rings the news of you all the way down the road, as proud as if she had found you herself.

choices.label: Head for the relay campfire

scene_relay_sing.narration: At night the centaur relay gathers at the biggest campfire to sing the route-songs: one verse for every landmark, the dangers in the chorus. This season the songs have new verses every night, faster than anyone can learn them. A centaur called Old Corran passes you the next line.

choices.label: Sing your verse
Just listen, very closely
Hear the verse the road crew made

check_sing.prompt: Sing a route-song verse in front of everybody

onSuccess.narration: Your voice wobbles once and then holds. The whole campfire sings the chorus back at you, and Old Corran thumps the ground with a hoof.

onFailure.narration: You sing the wrong verse, the one about a bridge three hundred miles away. Old Corran gently sings the right one over the top, and nobody minds at all.

scene_relay_sing_listen.narration: You sit very still and listen. Old Corran sings slowly, so you can follow. Verse after verse, landmark after landmark, and in every new verse the road bends away from somewhere. Away, and away, and away again. You begin to hear a shape in it.

choices.label: Ask Old Corran about the shape

scene_relay_sing_crew_verse.narration: Halfway through, the road crew from the detour come cantering in, and the road boss sings a brand new verse: about travelers who hauled marker posts and never once complained, much. It is about you. The whole campfire sings the chorus back. The road remembers.

choices.label: Listen to the rest of the verses

scene_spiral.narration: You hear the new verses sung in road order, and they are not random. Every new detour bends away from a place where stones fell. Sung end to end, the roads of the realm curl around the gemfalls like a snail shell. Old Corran scratches the new verses onto a strip of bark with a hoof-pick and gives it to you.

choices.label: Walk north under the stars

scene_ash_wind.narration: Walking north under the stars, a warm wind blows down from the mountain, full of gray ash as soft as moth dust. It glitters in your lantern light. Every gem in every pack on the road starts humming louder, all at once, as if the wind has said something they all agree with. Everybody vote.

choices.label: Pull up your collars and push on
Shelter behind a Skywarden supply wagon
Fly above the ash and look north

check_ash_wind.prompt: Lean into the ash wind and keep walking

onSuccess.narration: You link arms and march on through the glitter. It is like walking through warm gray snow. By the time the wind passes, you are gray from head to toe and look like a row of statues, and the bend in the road is just ahead.

onFailure.narration: The wind shoves you sideways into a hedge, one after another, like skittles. It is warm in the hedge, so you wait it out there, sneezing ash. When it passes you climb out, grayer and wiser, and the bend in the road is just ahead.

scene_ash_wind_shelter.narration: You duck behind a Skywarden supply wagon and find Sergeant Holloway already there, writing by lantern. "Ash wind," says the sergeant. "Third this week. Wind from the mountain means the mountain is busy." Holloway writes BUSY, underlines it twice, and offers you each a very dry biscuit.

choices.label: Walk on when the wind drops

scene_ash_wind_fly_above.narration: Your griffin climbs above the ash into clear starlight. Below, the rush's lanterns stretch north in one long glowing line. And the line is not straight. It curls around and around, bending away from dark patches, exactly like the verses on the bark. The whole road is singing the spiral with its feet.

choices.label: Glide back down to the road

scene_road_bend.narration: Plains folk say never camp where the road bends, because the road knows something. At the bend, a pack of cinder wolves is pacing back and forth across the road, glowing faintly, between you and tonight's camp.

choices.label: Wait quietly until they pass
Sneak around them through the long grass
Drive them off the road

check_sneak.prompt: Creep through the long grass without a rustle

onSuccess.narration: Not one blade of grass rustles. One wolf lifts its nose, sniffs, and goes back to pacing.

onFailure.narration: A jackalope pops out of the grass right in front of you, shouts its little jackalope shout, and every wolf turns your way.

encounter_wolves.narration: The wolves are cold and hungry and a long way from home, and they would like this bit of road, please.

onVictory.narration: The pack backs off into the grass and trots away north, toward the hills, glowing like a string of lanterns.

onDefeat.narration: The pack bowls through your camp, and everyone scatters in the dark.

scene_road_bend_wait.narration: You sit down in the road and wait, very quietly. The wolves pace, and pace, and then one by one they lift their noses toward the mountain and trot off north into the dark, glowing like a string of lanterns going home. Not one of them comes anywhere near your packs.

choices.label: Make camp past the bend

end_foothills_in_sight.narration: You make camp past the bend, where it is safe. To the north, in the morning light, you can see the red foothills, and the line where the rush is heading. The bark strip of verses is in your pack, and you know now what the whole road is quietly saying: it is not the eruption the land is flinching from. It is the stones.

end_scattered.narration: By the time you find each other again, it is almost morning. The wolves have eaten the supplies and run off north, and Sergeant Holloway's patrol finds you and writes you down in the ledger as 'Stragglers, Muddy'. You have lost a day, but the bark strip of verses is safe, and you are all together.

llmHints.tone: road country in full flood; noisy, kind, a little melancholy on the downbound lane, a little spooky at night, never scary

npcVoices.drover: the lead drover from the ford; huge booming voice, calls the party 'mudlarks'
npcVoices.ma_ruddle: a sold-out prospector; tired, blunt, cares about Tib and nothing else
npcVoices.tib: a small boy in an orange hat; talks to horses, ponies and centaurs as equals
npcVoices.wend: a Deep Hollow ladler; gentle, generous, remembers every name, certain the world can be fixed at the root
npcVoices.sergeant_holloway: a Skywarden supply sergeant; rigid, honest, calls everything 'arithmetic', writes everything down
npcVoices.clerk_pennywhistle: a depot clerk; loves forms, horrified by smudges, very sorry about Form 7B
npcVoices.old_corran: an old centaur relay singer; slow, warm, sings more than he speaks
npcVoices.road_boss: a centaur road-crew boss; brisk and practical, a marker post on each shoulder, says 'a road goes where the walking goes'
npcVoices.map_seller: a map seller in a velvet coat; smooth, cheerful, never technically lies
npcVoices.rumor_ring: noon-stop travelers swapping news; eager, garbled, every story a little bigger each time
